name: Dummy Deck
description: Sandbox for testing new technical phrases before migration.

cards.sideA: Cuando A es diferente de B, podemos acceder.

sideB.text: When A is different from B, we can access it.
When A differs from B, we can gain access.
We can access it when A is different from B.
When A is different to B, we can access it.

cards.note: ~When A is different from B, we can access~ is missing an object. The verb [access] is transitive in English and requires a direct object (e.g., [access it], [gain access]).

cards.sideA: Las devoluciones usan bandejas.

sideB.text: Returns use flats.
Returns are processed using flats.
Flats are used for returns.
Returns use trays.

cards.note: In logistics and mail sorting, a [flat] refers to a large envelope, magazine, or a flat sorting tray. A [tray] is a shallow container used to hold, sort, or carry items.

cards.sideA: No construyas las vistas que quedan aún.

sideB.text: Don't build the remaining views yet.
Do not build the views that are still left.
Don't build the views that are left yet.

cards.note:
**[er:108]**

~...that are leave yet~ is incorrect because 'leave' is a base verb. To express 'quedan' in this context, use the past participle [left].

cards.sideA: ¿Cuál sería el tiempo estimado de llegada de los arreglos?

sideB.text: What is the ETA for the fixes?
What is the Estimated Time of Arrival for the fixes?
What is the estimated completion time for the fixes?

cards.note: ~What will it be the ETA~ is incorrect because it uses a double subject. You must drop 'it' and say [What will the ETA be] or [What will be the ETA].

cards.sideA: compileSdkVersion indica la versión de Android con la que se compila la app.

sideB.text: compileSdkVersion sets the Android version used to compile the app.
compileSdkVersion indicates which Android version the app is compiled with.
compileSdkVersion defines the Android version that compiles the app.
compileSdkVersion defines the Android version against which the app is compiled.

cards.note:
**[er:104]**

~...sets the Android version is compiled the app~ lacks the proper sentence structure. It needs a relative clause and a preposition at the end, such as [the Android version the app is compiled with].

~...against the app is compiled~ is missing the relative pronoun. You must use [against which the app is compiled].

~...sets the Android version with the app gets compiled~ is missing a relative pronoun. You must say [with which the app gets compiled] or leave the preposition at the end: [the app gets compiled with].

cards.sideA: targetSdkVersion define la versión de Android para la que está optimizada la app.

sideB.text: targetSdkVersion defines the Android version the app is optimized for.
targetSdkVersion sets the Android version the app targets.
targetSdkVersion specifies which Android version the app is optimized for.

cards.note: ~...the app is optimized~ is missing the preposition at the end. It must be [optimized for] because the verb phrase is 'to optimize for'.

cards.sideA: Gradle gestiona las dependencias y las tareas de compilación.

sideB.text: Gradle manages dependencies and compilation tasks.
Gradle handles dependencies and build tasks.
Gradle takes care of dependencies and compilation tasks.
Gradle manages dependencies and building tasks.

cards.sideA: Android Gradle Plugin es la extensión de compilación que adapta Gradle para compilar y empaquetar aplicaciones Android.

sideB.text: The Android Gradle Plugin is the build extension that adapts Gradle to compile and package Android apps.
AGP is the build extension that lets Gradle compile and package Android applications.
The Android Gradle Plugin extends Gradle so it can compile and package Android apps.

cards.sideA: Usando 0.1 de opacidad significa que el color es casi totalmente transparente.

sideB.text: Using 0.1 opacity means the color is almost completely transparent.
An opacity of 0.1 makes the color nearly fully transparent.
Setting the opacity to 0.1 leaves the color almost invisible.

cards.note:
~Using 0.1 of opacity~ is unnatural because in English we omit the preposition and say [0.1 opacity], or use the structure [an opacity of 0.1].

In mathematics and decimals, the '.' symbol is pronounced as [point] (e.g., zero point one). The word [dot] is used for web addresses and file extensions (like .com or .json).

cards.sideA: Con opacidad baja el elemento es más transparente y se ve menos.

sideB.text: Low opacity makes the element more transparent and less visible.
With low opacity the element looks more transparent and harder to see.
The lower the opacity, the more transparent and less visible the element becomes.

cards.sideA: El contenedor envuelve la lista y elimina los huecos.

sideB.text: The container wraps the list and removes the gaps.
The container wraps around the list and gets rid of the gaps.
The container wraps the list, removing the gaps.
The container wraps the list and deletes the gaps.

cards.sideA: Este componente envuelve la imagen para que no queden huecos.

sideB.text: This component wraps the image so there are no gaps.
This component wraps around the image to avoid any gaps.
This component wraps the image so that no gaps are left.
This component wraps the image to not have gaps.
This component wraps the image to not leave any gaps.

cards.note:
**[er:188]**

[Gap] means an empty space or opening between two objects or elements.

cards.sideA: Vamos a probar primero el happy path de esta función.

sideB.text: Let's test the happy path of this feature first.
First, we are going to test the happy path of this feature.
Let's start by testing the happy path for this feature.
Let's first test the happy path of this feature.

cards.sideA: ¿No debería ser todo al mismo tiempo, como en la versión Mobile?

sideB.text: Shouldn't it all be at the same time, like in the Mobile version?
Shouldn't everything happen at once, like in the Mobile version?
Shouldn't it all be at the same time, the way it is in the Mobile version?
Shouldn't it be all at the same time, like in the Mobile version?

cards.sideA: Esta inversión produce un alto rendimiento cada año.

sideB.text: This investment yields a high return every year.
This investment produces a high return each year.
This investment delivers a high yield every year.

cards.sideA: El cálculo arroja el resultado correcto.

sideB.text: The calculation yields the correct result.
The calculation returns the correct result.
The calculation gives the right result.
The calculation generates the correct result.
The calculation produces the correct result.

cards.note: ~The calculate yields...~ is incorrect because 'calculate' is a verb. You must use the noun form [calculation].

cards.sideA: Calentar agua genera vapor.

sideB.text: Heating water yields steam.
Heating water produces steam.
Heating up water generates steam.

cards.note:
~Heating water yields stream~ contains a spelling mistake. A 'stream' is a flow of water (arroyo) or data (flujo), whereas the correct word for 'vapor' is [steam].

~Heat water yields steam~ uses a bare verb as the subject, which reads as an order followed by a second verb. When an action is the subject of the sentence it must be a gerund: [Heating water yields steam].

cards.sideA: Por favor, concatena tu nombre y apellido.

sideB.text: Please concatenate your first and last name.
Please join your first name and your last name together.
Please concatenate your first name with your surname.

cards.sideA: El sistema concatenará los códigos de error.

sideB.text: The system will concatenate the error codes.
The system is going to concatenate the error codes.
The error codes will be concatenated by the system.

cards.sideA: Puedes concatenar estos archivos de texto fácilmente.

sideB.text: You can concatenate these text files easily.
You can easily concatenate these text files.
These text files can be concatenated easily.

cards.sideA: Ya no deberían ver más el mensaje de advertencia.

sideB.text: You should not see the warning message anymore.
You shouldn't be seeing the warning message any more.
The warning message should not show up for you again.
You should not see the warning message any longer.

cards.note:
~You should not see more the warning messagr~ is not valid because 'more' is placed incorrectly. The correct phrasing uses [anymore] or [any more] at the end of the sentence.

~You should not see any longer the warning message~ has an incorrect word order. The adverbial phrase [any longer] must be placed at the very end of the sentence or clause: [You should not see the warning message any longer].

cards.sideA: El mensaje de advertencia desapareció!

sideB.text: The warning message is gone!
The warning message disappeared!
The warning message went away!

cards.sideA: Es el punto de entrada a la app para Android, cada ambiente tiene uno.

sideB.text: It is the entry point to the Android app, every environment has one.
It's the entry point of the Android app, and each environment has its own.
That is the Android app entry point, and there is one per environment.
It is the starting point to the Android app, every environment has one.

cards.sideA: MainActivity es una clase de Android, y se necesita declarar para cada ambiente.

sideB.text: MainActivity is an Android class, and it needs to be declared for each environment.
MainActivity is an Android class, and you need to declare it for every environment.
MainActivity is an Android class that has to be declared per environment.

cards.sideA: API 36 es Android 16, API 35 es Android 15, y así...

sideB.text: API 36 is Android 16, API 35 is Android 15, and so on.
API 36 means Android 16, API 35 means Android 15, and so on.
API level 36 maps to Android 16, API level 35 maps to Android 15, and so forth.

cards.sideA: API 34 es Android 14, API 33 es Android 13, y así...

sideB.text: API 34 is Android 14, API 33 is Android 13, and so on.
API 34 corresponds to Android 14, API 33 corresponds to Android 13, and so on.
API level 34 is Android 14, API level 33 is Android 13, and so forth.

cards.sideA: Es el archivo que abre la app cuando el usuario toca el icono.

sideB.text: It's the file that opens the app when the user taps the icon.
It is the file that launches the app when the user taps the icon.
That file is what opens the app once the user taps on the icon.

cards.sideA: Es la versión de Android contra la que la app se construye y se prueba.

sideB.text: It's the Android version the app is built and tested against.
It is the Android version that the app is compiled and tested against.
That's the Android version used to build and test the app.

cards.note: ~It is the Android version against the app is compiled and tested~ is missing the relative pronoun. A preposition placed before the clause requires [which]: [the Android version against which the app is compiled and tested]. The natural spoken option is to leave the preposition at the end: [the Android version the app is compiled and tested against].

cards.sideA: NDK significa Native Development Kit.

sideB.text: NDK stands for Native Development Kit.
NDK means Native Development Kit.
The acronym NDK stands for Native Development Kit.

cards.sideA: Gradle es la herramienta que construye la app de Android.

sideB.text: Gradle is the tool that builds the Android app.
Gradle is the build tool for the Android app.
The Android app is built by Gradle.

cards.sideA: Kotlin es el lenguaje en el que está escrito el lado Android de la app.

sideB.text: Kotlin is the language the Android side of the app is written in.
Kotlin is the language used to write the Android side of the app.
The Android side of the app is written in Kotlin.

cards.note:
~...the Android app is written~ is incomplete. You must include the preposition [in] at the end: [is written in].

~Kotlin is the language written in the Android side of the app~ reverses the meaning: it says the language itself was written inside the Android side. What gets written is the code, so the relative clause must keep its own subject: [the language the Android side of the app is written in].

cards.sideA: La correspondencia de Gradle en iOS se gestiona directamente en Xcode.

sideB.text: On iOS, the equivalent of Gradle is handled directly in Xcode.
The iOS counterpart of Gradle is handled directly inside Xcode.
On iOS, whatever Gradle does is managed straight from Xcode.

cards.note: ~...the corresponcy of Gradle~ is incorrect because 'corresponcy' is not a valid word. The correct terms are [equivalent] or [counterpart].

cards.sideA: El monto de crédito solo se calcula si la responsabilidad tiene los créditos activados.

sideB.text: The credit amount is only calculated if the responsibility has credits enabled.
The credit amount is calculated only when the responsibility has credits turned on.
We only calculate the credit amount if credits are enabled for the responsibility.
The credit amount is only calculated if the responsibility has credits activated.

cards.sideA: Los créditos son opcionales, así que leemos el perfil XXSBL_IBE_USE_CREDITS antes de mostrarlos.

sideB.text: Credits are optional, so we read the XXSBL_IBE_USE_CREDITS profile option before showing them.
Credits are optional, so we check the XXSBL_IBE_USE_CREDITS profile option before displaying them.
Since credits are optional, we read the profile option XXSBL_IBE_USE_CREDITS first and only then show them.

cards.sideA: Es el mismo control que ya está en GET_CREDIT_AMOUNT.

sideB.text: It is the same check already in GET_CREDIT_AMOUNT.
It's the same validation that is already in GET_CREDIT_AMOUNT.
This is the same check we already have inside GET_CREDIT_AMOUNT.

cards.sideA: Android usa CircularProgressIndicator, iOS usa CupertinoActivityIndicator.

sideB.text: Android uses CircularProgressIndicator, iOS uses CupertinoActivityIndicator.
On Android we use CircularProgressIndicator, and on iOS we use CupertinoActivityIndicator.
Android relies on CircularProgressIndicator while iOS relies on CupertinoActivityIndicator.

cards.sideA: El código elige el spinner según la plataforma en la que corre.

sideB.text: The code picks the spinner based on the platform it runs on.
The code chooses the spinner depending on the platform it is running on.
Which spinner is used depends on the platform the code runs on.

cards.note:
~...based on the platform it runs~ is incomplete. You must include the preposition [on] at the end to specify where it runs: [it runs on].

In this context, 'run on' is not a true phrasal verb. It is simply the verb [run] (to execute or operate) followed by the preposition [on] indicating the platform or surface. The core meaning of the verb does not change idiomatically as it would in a real phrasal verb like 'run out' or 'run into'.

cards.sideA: Cada plataforma usa su propio estilo de spinner nativo.

sideB.text: Each platform uses its own native spinner style.
Every platform has its own native spinner style.
Each platform shows the spinner in its own native style.

cards.sideA: VSCode es solo el editor donde escribo el código; quien compila es Android y Xcode por detrás.

sideB.text: VSCode is only the editor where I write the code; Android and Xcode do the compiling behind it.
VSCode is just the editor I write the code in; the actual compiling is done by Android and Xcode.
I only use VSCode to write the code; Android and Xcode are the ones compiling in the background.
VSCode is only the editor where I write the code; it's Android and Xcode that compile behind it.

cards.note:
~...who compiles is Android and Xcode behind it~ is incorrect because 'who' is used for people. For tools or programs, use [what compiles] or [the ones that compile].

~It's Android and Xcode that compiles behind it~ fails the agreement. The focus of the cleft is two tools, so the verb stays plural: [it's Android and Xcode that compile behind it].

~It's Android and Xcode they ones that compiled behind it~ mixes two different structures and puts the verb in the past. Choose one: [it's Android and Xcode that compile behind it] or [Android and Xcode are the ones that compile behind it].

cards.sideA: Uso VSCode para editar, pero el build real lo hacen las herramientas de Android y de Xcode.

sideB.text: I use VSCode to edit, but the real build is done by Android's and Xcode's tools.
I use VSCode to edit, but the actual build is handled by the Android and Xcode tools.
The editing happens in VSCode, but the Android and Xcode tools do the real build.

cards.note: ~I use VSCode to edit, but the real build are made by tools like Android and Xcode.~ is incorrect because the noun 'build' is singular, meaning it requires a singular verb like [is made] or [is done]. Additionally, [is done by] is much more natural here than 'made by'.

cards.sideA: VSCode no compila nada por sí solo; llama a las herramientas de Android y de Xcode para generar el binario.

sideB.text: VSCode does not compile anything by itself; it calls Android's and Xcode's tools to produce the binary.
VSCode does not compile anything on its own; it calls the Android and Xcode tools to build the binary.
By itself VSCode compiles nothing; it invokes the Android and Xcode tools to generate the binary.

cards.note: ~...by its own~ is a mix of two expressions. You must use either [on its own] or [by itself].

cards.sideA: Ese vacío heredado ya no ocurre; esta línea lo restaura.

sideB.text: That inherited blank state no longer happens; this line restores it.
That inherited empty state does not happen anymore; this line resets it.
The inherited blank value no longer occurs, because this line restores it.

cards.note:
~That inherited gap no longer happens~ changes the meaning. In programming, 'vacío' refers to a [blank state] or [empty value], whereas 'gap' refers to physical or temporal space.

~That inherited blank state is no longer happened~ puts an intransitive verb into the passive. 'Happen' never takes a passive form because nobody performs it on something else: [no longer happens] or [does not happen anymore].

cards.sideA: El error ocurría con clientes dummy cuando no tenían fechas de pedido.

sideB.text: The bug happened with dummy customers when they had no order dates.
The bug showed up with dummy customers that had no order dates.
The error occurred for dummy customers whenever they had no order dates.
The bug happened when dummy customers didn't have order dates.

cards.sideA: Si un cliente no tenía fechas de pedido, ese vacío pasaba al siguiente cliente.

sideB.text: If a customer had no order dates, that blank state passed to the next customer.
If a customer had no order dates, that empty state carried over to the next customer.
When a customer had no order dates, the blank value leaked into the next customer.
If a customer didn't have order dates, that blank state passed to the next customer.

cards.sideA: Estamos revisando los problemas de lentitud.

sideB.text: We are looking into the slowness issues.
We are currently investigating the performance issues.
We are checking the slowness problems right now.

cards.note: ~We are checking the slow problems right now~ is not natural. We use the noun [slowness] or [performance] to describe the issue, rather than the adjective 'slow'.

cards.sideA: La lentitud se debe a llamadas al backend que tardan mucho en regresar.

sideB.text: The slowness is caused by backend calls that take a long time to come back.
The slowness is due to backend calls that take too long to respond.
It is slow because the backend calls take a long time to return.
The slowness is due to backend calls that are taking too long.

cards.note: ~...take a long time in return~ uses a fixed expression that means 'a cambio', not 'en regresar'. After 'take a long time' the verb goes in the infinitive: [to return] or [to come back].

cards.sideA: El equivalente de Google Play Console en Android, es App Store en iOS.

sideB.text: The equivalent of Google Play Console on Android is the App Store on iOS.
On iOS, the App Store is the equivalent of Google Play Console on Android.
Google Play Console on Android is the equivalent of the App Store on iOS.
The equivalent of Google Play Console for Android is the App Store for iOS.

cards.sideA: El equivalente de Play Store para Android, es App Store para iOS.

sideB.text: The equivalent of the Play Store for Android is the App Store for iOS.
For iOS, the App Store is the equivalent of the Play Store for Android.
The Play Store for Android is equivalent to the App Store for iOS.
The equivalent of the Play Store on Android is the App Store on iOS.
